newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were mostly steady, instances $0.50 per cwt higher in the eastern Corn Belt, underpinned by light marketings and strong regional demand, livestock dealers said.
"We've got a couple of packers short on hogs this morning so they're pushing hard for them," one Illinois dealer said.

Illinois hogs sold $0.50 higher at $57.50 to $58.00 in the country and $58.50 to $59.00 at plants, with several packers willing to pay $59.50 to $60.00 for top quality hogs delivered to the plant, the dealer said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $57.50 to $58.00 in the country and $58.50 to $59.00 at plants, dealers and packer buyers there said. Demand was light for weekend slaughter, but marketings also were light so prices held steady, they said.
Indiana hogs sold steady in light volume at $57.00 to $57.50 in the country and $58.50 to $59.50 at plants.

Part of the light demand was tied to Indiana Packers Corp. (IPC) not slaughtering Friday at its Delphi, Ind., plant due to planned maintenance. Slaughter should resume on Monday, a company source said.
Delphi slaughters 10,000-12,000 hogs per day, IPC said.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $57.00 in the country and $58.00 to $59.00 at plant in thin activity.
